CODE
Art. 2.3.43.
Effects of dissolution 
The dissolution of the regime gives rise to liquidation and partition.
First, an account is drawn up for each spouse of the rewards between the joint patrimony and his or her own patrimony.
The liabilities are then settled, the account of rewards settled and the net assets divided.
The provisions of the Judicial Code concerning partition and auction and those of the Civil Code concerning the partition of successions are applicable.
For the following assets, the value at the time of the dissolution of the regime, and not at the time of the partition, is included in the assets to be partitioned: 
1¡ the asset value of the company shares referred to in Article 2.3.19, ¤ 1er , 5¡; 
2¡ the asset value of professional assets which have been acquired by one of the spouses with common funds, if the right to such professional assets is proprietary by virtue of Article 2.3.19, ¤ 1er , 6¡; 
3¡ the economic value of the clientele which was constituted or acquired during the regime by one of the spouses in the exercise of his profession or the operation of his business, if the right to this clientele is proprietary by virtue of Article 2.3.19, ¤ 1er , 7¡. ¤ 4.
The heirs of spouses have the same rights and are bound by the same obligations as the spouse they represent.
